content: Everything can be taken from a man but one thing: the last of the human freedoms - to choose one's attitude in any given set of circumstances.
author: Viktor Frankl
story: Stripped of his clinical career, his book manuscript, his clothes, and his loved ones across Auschwitz and Dachau, Viktor Frankl observed human behavior at the razor's edge of survival. While the SS guards possessed total power over the physical bodies of prisoners, Frankl discovered an unassailable sanctuary: the guards could never breach the inner freedom of consciousness. Even in the freezing mud of dawn roll-calls, a person retained the sovereign power to choose courage over despair and dignity over bitterness.
reflectionPrompt: What difficult circumstance do you currently feel constrained by, and what internal attitude can you choose right now that no outside power can take from you?
